title: Linkability of student submissions to other student data
description: Student ID, course, and submission timestamp in this flow can be linked to other student records (grades, attendance, previous submissions) to create comprehensive student profiles, potentially revealing patterns about study habits, performance trends, and personal circumstances.
assumptions: System maintains multiple data stores with student information that can be cross-referenced

title: Direct identifiability of student from submission data
description: Student ID is explicitly transmitted in the assignment submission, making the student directly identifiable. Combined with course and timestamp, this creates a clear identity trail for each submission.
assumptions: Student ID is a unique identifier that can be used to identify the individual student

title: Unauthorized disclosure of assignment content during transmission
description: Assignment work file, student ID, course information, and submission timestamp could be intercepted during transmission if the connection between student and Grades Portal is not properly secured (e.g., missing TLS/SSL encryption).
assumptions: Data is transmitted over network that could be vulnerable to interception

title: Data aggregation across multiple submissions
description: Multiple assignment submissions from the same student can be aggregated to analyze performance patterns, submission timing habits, and learning behaviors, potentially revealing sensitive information about the student's academic struggles or personal circumstances.
assumptions: System stores historical submission data that can be aggregated and analyzed

title: Data reaching unintended recipients
description: Assignment submission data may be forwarded to unintended recipients such as analytics services, logging systems, third-party integrations, or backup systems without the student's explicit knowledge or consent.
assumptions: System may have integrations with external services or logging mechanisms

title: Direct Identifiers Stored
description: The grading service stores student ID along with assignment files, creating a direct link between personal identity and academic work. This identifiability enables tracking of individual student performance and submission patterns.
assumptions: Student ID is a unique personal identifier that can be used to identify specific individuals

title: Unauthorized Access to Stored Assignments
description: Assignment files containing student work, IDs, and submission metadata stored in DS1 could be accessed by unauthorized parties if the data store lacks proper access controls, encryption, or security measures.
assumptions: Data store DS1 may have insufficient security controls protecting stored personal data

title: Excessive Data Collection for Storage
description: The grading service collects and stores student ID, course information, and submission time with assignment files. This may exceed the minimality principle if all this data is not strictly necessary for the grading function.
assumptions: Data minimization principles should apply to what is stored in the assignment repository
uncertainty_note: Uncertain whether all stored fields are strictly necessary for grading purposes

title: Student Unawareness of Data Storage
description: Students may not be fully aware that their assignment files, student IDs, and submission timestamps are being stored in a persistent data store, and for how long this data will be retained.
assumptions: Students may not have clear visibility into what data is stored and retention policies

title: Teacher identity processed during login
description: The teacher's identity is transmitted and processed by the Grades Portal Web App during authentication. This constitutes processing of identified data as the system must verify the teacher's credentials and identity to grant access.
assumptions: Standard authentication flow where teacher credentials are transmitted to the application

title: Teacher identity linked to review activities
description: The teacher's identity can be linked to their submission review activities, creating a profile of which courses they teach and which student submissions they review. This linkability could be used to infer teaching assignments and workload.
assumptions: System logs teacher identity with each submission review request

title: Teacher credentials exposed in transit
description: Teacher login credentials (username/password or tokens) could be intercepted during transmission from the teacher's device to the Grades Portal Web App, potentially allowing unauthorized access to the system.
assumptions: Credentials transmitted over network without adequate encryption

title: Teacher unaware of data collection scope
description: The teacher may not be fully aware of what data is being collected about their review activities, including timestamps, submission IDs reviewed, and time spent on reviews, which could be used for performance monitoring.
assumptions: Privacy policy does not clearly communicate all data collection practices

title: Linkability of student submissions to identities
description: An attacker intercepting this flow could link student names with their work content and submission times, enabling correlation of academic performance with specific students across multiple submissions.
assumptions: Flow is transmitted over network without adequate encryption or access controls

title: Direct identifiability of students
description: Student names are explicitly transmitted in this flow, making students directly identifiable if the data is exposed or intercepted.
assumptions: Student names are included in the data payload as described

title: Unauthorized disclosure of student work
description: Student submissions, names, and work content could be disclosed to unauthorized parties if the portal or transmission is compromised.
assumptions: Portal has access control vulnerabilities or transmission lacks encryption

title: Data aggregation revealing student patterns
description: Submission times, work content, and student names could be aggregated with other data sources to build detailed profiles of student behavior, performance patterns, and learning habits.
assumptions: Multiple data flows or external data sources exist that could be combined

title: Lack of student control over submission visibility
description: Students may have no control over which teachers can view their submissions, when they are displayed, or how long the data is retained in the portal.
assumptions: Portal does not provide student privacy controls or consent mechanisms

title: Linkability of grade records to student profiles
description: Student ID and grader ID in the grade submission can be linked to other data about the same student (e.g., other assignments, attendance, performance history) or teacher (grading patterns, other students graded), enabling comprehensive profiling.
assumptions: System maintains multiple data records per student and teacher that can be correlated

title: Direct identifiability of students and teachers
description: Student ID and grader ID directly identify specific individuals in the grade submission, making this personally identifiable information (PII) that requires protection.
assumptions: Student ID and grader ID are unique identifiers that can be mapped to real individuals

title: Non-repudiation of grade submission
description: Without proper audit logging, a teacher could deny having submitted a particular grade or feedback, creating accountability issues and potential disputes.
assumptions: System may not maintain immutable audit trails of grade submissions

title: Unauthorized disclosure of grades and feedback
description: Grades and written feedback are sensitive academic information that could be intercepted during transmission from teacher to the web application if not properly encrypted.
assumptions: Data transmission may not be encrypted or could be vulnerable to interception

title: Data aggregation revealing performance patterns
description: Multiple grade submissions can be aggregated to reveal student performance trends, teacher grading patterns, or comparative analysis that may not be intended for public disclosure.
assumptions: System stores multiple grade records that can be queried and combined

title: Student lack of control over grade data
description: Students have no control over what grade or feedback information teachers submit about them, and may not be able to review, correct, or delete this data once submitted.
assumptions: Students cannot modify or control grade records submitted by teachers

title: Unauthorized Disclosure of Grade Records
description: Grade records containing student id, course, grade, feedback, grader id, and timestamp could be accessed by unauthorized parties through the database, leading to privacy violations of sensitive academic information.
assumptions: Database has access controls that could be bypassed or misconfigured

title: Student Identifiability in Grade Records
description: Grade records contain direct identifiers (student id) that can be used to identify individual students, creating privacy risks if records are exposed or improperly accessed.
assumptions: Student IDs are persistent identifiers that can be linked to real identities

title: Grade Data Aggregation for Student Profiling
description: Multiple grade records stored in the database can be aggregated to build comprehensive academic profiles of students, potentially revealing patterns beyond what was intended for individual course assessment.
assumptions: Database allows querying across multiple records and courses

title: Linkability of Grade Records to Other Student Data
description: Grade records with student id can be linked to other student data systems (enrollment, financial, disciplinary records) creating comprehensive student profiles that may exceed privacy expectations.
assumptions: Student IDs are used consistently across multiple systems

title: Non-compliance with Grade Data Privacy Regulations
description: Storage of grade records may not comply with educational privacy regulations (e.g., FERPA) regarding data retention, access controls, or student rights to access/correct their records.
assumptions: System may not have implemented all required privacy compliance measures
uncertainty_note: Specific regulatory requirements depend on jurisdiction and institution policies

title: Processing of identified student data
description: The Grades Portal Web App processes personally identifiable student information when handling grade requests. The student's identity is explicitly known and linked to their academic records.
assumptions: Student authentication is required to access grades

title: Unauthorized disclosure of grades
description: Student grades and feedback could be disclosed to unauthorized parties during transmission or processing. Grade data is highly sensitive and protected under educational privacy regulations.
assumptions: Grades contain sensitive academic performance information

title: Non-compliance with educational privacy regulations
description: The flow may not comply with FERPA or other educational privacy regulations governing student record access and disclosure. Proper authorization and audit logging may be required.
assumptions: Educational institution is subject to FERPA or similar regulations
uncertainty_note: Regulatory requirements may vary by jurisdiction

title: Data integrity compromise of grades
description: Grade data could be modified or corrupted during transmission from student request to processing, potentially affecting academic records accuracy.
assumptions: Grades are stored and transmitted digitally

title: Unauthorized disclosure of grades and feedback
description: If the data flow from the Grades Portal to the student is intercepted (e.g., via network eavesdropping, man-in-the-middle attack, or compromised endpoint), the student's grades and teacher feedback could be disclosed to unauthorized parties. This is sensitive educational data that should only be accessible to the student and authorized personnel.
assumptions: The flow transmits over a network that could potentially be monitored or intercepted

title: Identifiability through grades data
description: The grades and feedback transmitted in this flow contain personally identifiable information about the student. If intercepted, this data could be used to identify the student and link the information to their identity, especially if combined with other data sources.
assumptions: Grades and feedback are unique enough to identify the student when combined with other available information

title: Lack of non-repudiation for grade delivery
description: Without proper logging and audit trails, there may be no proof that the student actually received their grades and feedback. This could lead to disputes where the student claims they never received certain feedback, or the institution cannot prove delivery.
assumptions: The system may not implement comprehensive logging of data delivery to students

title: Potential non-compliance with educational data regulations
description: Grades are sensitive educational data that may be protected under regulations like FERPA (in the US) or similar data protection laws. Improper handling, transmission, or storage of this data in the flow could result in regulatory non-compliance.
assumptions: The system operates in a jurisdiction with educational data protection regulations
uncertainty_note: Regulatory requirements vary by jurisdiction; this assumes applicable educational data protection laws exist

title: Linkability of parent login to child grade data
description: Parent's authentication credentials and grade request can be linked to identify which parent is accessing which child's grades, creating a linkable record of parent-child relationships and academic performance.
assumptions: System logs authentication and data access events

title: Identifiability of parent and child through grade access
description: Parent login credentials and child account linkage enable identification of both parent and child through the grade request flow.
assumptions: Parent account is linked to specific child account in system

title: Disclosure of grades during transmission
description: Child's grades transmitted from Grades Portal Web App to parent could be intercepted if connection is not properly secured (e.g., missing TLS/HTTPS).
assumptions: Data transmitted over network between parent device and web app

title: Non-repudiation of grade access request
description: Parent could deny having requested child's grades if system lacks proper audit logging of access requests.
assumptions: System may or may not maintain detailed access logs

title: Data aggregation through repeated grade access
description: Multiple grade access requests over time could be aggregated to build profiles of parent engagement patterns or child academic performance trends.
assumptions: System retains historical access data

title: Unauthorized access to child grades
description: If authentication/authorization controls are weak, unauthorized parties could access the child's grades, feedback, and submission history through this portal flow.
assumptions: Assumes proper access controls should be in place for parent verification

title: Potential violation of educational data privacy regulations
description: Displaying grades without proper parent verification could violate FERPA (US) or GDPR (EU) requirements for educational data protection.
assumptions: Assumes regulatory requirements for educational data apply to this system

title: Potential identification of child-parent relationships
description: If authentication is weak, unauthorized parties could identify which child belongs to which parent through this grades portal flow.
assumptions: Assumes proper authentication is in place for parent access

title: Direct Identifiers in Account Management
description: Administrator transmits names and email addresses when creating/modifying accounts, enabling direct identification of students and parents.
assumptions: Names and emails are transmitted in clear or insufficiently protected form

title: Unauthorized Disclosure of Personal Data
description: Account data (names, emails, roles, parent-child relationships) could be intercepted or accessed by unauthorized parties during transmission or at the process boundary.
assumptions: Transmission channel may lack adequate encryption or access controls

title: Linkability of Account Data to Other Records
description: Account creation/modification data can be linked to other student/parent records in the system, enabling comprehensive profiling.
assumptions: System maintains multiple data stores with overlapping identifiers

title: Aggregation of Relationship Data
description: Multiple parent-child link modifications could be aggregated to reveal family structures and relationships beyond what individuals expect to share.
assumptions: Multiple account modifications occur over time and can be correlated

title: Non-repudiation of Administrative Actions
description: Administrator account modifications (create, modify, disable) may lack proper audit trails, allowing actions to be denied later.
assumptions: System may not maintain comprehensive, tamper-proof logs of administrative actions

title: Unawareness of Account Modifications
description: Parents/students may not be notified when their accounts or relationships are modified by administrators, violating transparency expectations.
assumptions: No notification mechanism exists for account changes

title: Regulatory Compliance Risk
description: Processing of personal data (names, emails, relationships) may not comply with FERPA, GDPR, or other privacy regulations if proper legal basis and consent are not established.
assumptions: Administrative account management may lack documented legal basis for processing
uncertainty_note: Depends on specific jurisdiction and consent mechanisms in place

title: Linkability of student accounts with parent accounts
description: The Account Directory stores parent-child relationship links alongside account records, enabling correlation between student and parent identities. This creates linkability that could reveal family relationships and associated grading information.
assumptions: Parent-child relationship data is stored in a way that can be queried or accessed

title: Identifiability of students and parents in account records
description: Account records written to the Account Directory contain identifiable information about students and parents, which could be used to identify individuals if the data store is compromised or accessed without authorization.
assumptions: Account records contain personally identifiable information

title: Unauthorized disclosure of account and relationship data
description: Account records and parent-child relationship links stored in the Account Directory could be disclosed to unauthorized parties through data breaches, insider threats, or inadequate access controls.
assumptions: Data store has access control mechanisms that could be bypassed

title: Data aggregation enabling profiling
description: The Account Directory aggregates account records and relationship links, which could be combined with other data sources to create detailed profiles of students and families, potentially revealing sensitive patterns.
assumptions: Multiple data sources could be correlated with account directory data

title: Unawareness of data storage and relationship tracking
description: Students and parents may not be aware that their account records and parent-child relationships are being stored in the Account Directory, or the extent of data being collected and retained.
assumptions: Privacy notices may not clearly explain data storage practices

title: Non-compliance with educational privacy regulations
description: Storage of student account records and parent-child relationships may not comply with educational privacy regulations such as FERPA, particularly regarding data retention, access controls, and parental consent requirements.
assumptions: Educational institution is subject to FERPA or similar regulations
uncertainty_note: Regulatory compliance depends on specific jurisdiction and institutional policies

title: Data Disclosure to Third-Party Cloud Provider
description: Full grade records, assignments, and account directory containing personal student data are transferred to an external cloud hosting provider for backup and replication. This represents explicit data disclosure across a system boundary to a third party.
assumptions: The cloud hosting provider is considered outside the system boundary as an ExternalEntity

title: Increased Identifiability via Third-Party Storage
description: Account directory and grade records sent to cloud provider contain personally identifiable information. Storing this data with a third party increases identifiability risks if the provider's security is compromised or if data is accessed by unauthorized personnel.
assumptions: Account directory contains PII such as student names, IDs, or contact information

title: Linkability Across Data Sources
description: Cloud hosting provider may combine this student data with other datasets they hold, enabling linking of student information across different contexts or services, potentially revealing more about students than intended.
assumptions: Cloud provider may have access to or collect other data that could be linked with this student data
uncertainty_note: Depends on cloud provider's data practices and whether they aggregate data from multiple clients

title: Student Unawareness of Data Transfer
description: Students may not be aware that their grade records, assignments, and account information are being transferred to a third-party cloud hosting provider for backup purposes.
assumptions: Privacy notices may not clearly communicate third-party data transfers for backup

title: Lack of Control Over Third-Party Data Handling
description: Once data is transferred to the cloud hosting provider, students and the institution have limited control over how the provider stores, processes, or secures the data, including potential sub-processing to other vendors.
assumptions: Standard cloud service agreements may limit customer control over data handling practices

title: Grade records linkable to student identities
description: Grade records in DS2 contain student identifiers that could be linked across different contexts (student, parent, teacher views) to build comprehensive profiles of individual students' academic performance.
assumptions: Grade records contain student identifiers and are accessed by the grading service to build multiple views

title: Student identifiability from grade records
description: Grade records may contain or enable inference of student identities when accessed by the grading service, potentially exposing sensitive academic information to unauthorized parties.
assumptions: Grade records contain personally identifiable information or can be linked to student identities

title: Unauthorized disclosure of grade information
description: Grade records being read by the grading service could be disclosed to unauthorized parties if access controls are insufficient or if the service is compromised.
assumptions: Grade records contain sensitive academic performance data requiring protection

title: Data aggregation across student views
description: The grading service aggregates grade data to build student, parent, and teacher views, which could reveal patterns or information beyond what individual users should access.
assumptions: Multiple views are built from the same grade records, potentially enabling cross-view inference

title: Unawareness of grade data processing
description: Students, parents, or teachers may not be aware of how their grade data is being accessed, processed, and shared by the grading service across different views.
assumptions: Users may not have clear visibility into data processing activities
